patterns.note: Generous vertical spacing between major content sections, creating an airy and unhurried reading experience.
A strong contrast between elegant, oversized serif headings and clean, understated sans-serif body text, giving an editorial feel.
A minimalist palette of off-white backgrounds and dark text is punctuated by rich, muted earthy tones in hero and product imagery.

The initial top bar disappears on scroll, and the main navigation becomes a sticky header. The hero image content appears to parallax, scrolling slower than the text overlay, creating a layered depth effect.
Content is presented in distinct, full-width sections, often centered, with ample whitespace above and below each block.

technique_notes: The site employs a sticky header that activates after a short scroll distance, where an initial top bar disappears and the main navigation remains fixed at the top of the viewport, gaining a solid background.

The hero section features a subtle parallax effect where the background image scrolls at a slower rate than the foreground text and subsequent content, creating a sense of depth as the user scrolls down.
Typography is structured with a large, elegant serif font for primary headings and a clean, legible sans-serif for body text and navigation, emphasizing a sophisticated, editorial aesthetic.

design_tokens.type_scale: Oversized, elegant serif headings (~3-4x body) with smaller, clean sans-serif body and uppercase labels.
design_tokens.radius: Subtle for interactive elements like buttons, sharp for most imagery and structural elements.
design_tokens.spacing: Very airy, particularly vertical spacing between sections and within the hero, creating a sense of luxury and breathing room.

standout: The site's distinctive use of art-directed, editorial photography combined with a classic, elegant serif typeface for headings creates a high-end, magazine-like aesthetic that feels more like a curated experience than a typical e-commerce site. The subtle hero parallax adds to this sophisticated feel.
